paper_cards.title: SmolVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model for Affordable and Efficient Robotics
paper_cards.data: LeRobot/community-style robot data and VLA evaluation settings reported by the paper/project page.
paper_cards.method: Compact VLA model designed for affordable and efficient robotics, with a smaller vision-language backbone and action-generation component.
paper_cards.task: Language-conditioned robot manipulation and generalist visuomotor control under efficiency constraints.
paper_cards.novelty: Shows that useful VLA capability can be pursued with smaller, more deployable models rather than only large closed systems.
paper_cards.evidence: Primary arXiv paper and Hugging Face paper page report competitive performance with reduced training and inference cost.

claim_checks.claim: SmolVLA is an efficient VLA model for robotics.
claim_checks.notes: Primary source found; detailed benchmark and demo claims still need PDF-level verification before acceptance.

claim_checks.claim: LeRobot ecosystem provides relevant code context.
claim_checks.notes: Repository exists; exact SmolVLA release/checkpoint status was not verified in this dry run.

paper_cards.limitations: Dry-run did not reproduce experiments; detailed benchmark numbers need deep-read verification before registry application.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Relevant to the VLA branch because deployable VLA models are likely downstream consumers of interactive generated worlds.
claims_requiring_verification: Exact benchmark scores and model size should be checked in the PDF before applying registry patch.

paper_cards.title: OpenEQA: Embodied Question Answering in the Era of Foundation Models
paper_cards.data: Embodied question-answering benchmark over physical/scanned environments with natural-language questions.
paper_cards.method: Benchmark formulation for open-vocabulary embodied QA in the foundation-model era.
paper_cards.task: Answer questions about an environment from embodied or environment-level observations.
paper_cards.novelty: Modernizes EQA as open-vocabulary evaluation of environment understanding rather than closed-set QA only.
paper_cards.evidence: CVPR 2024 paper page and project page provide primary benchmark source.

claim_checks.claim: OpenEQA is a CVPR 2024 embodied QA benchmark.
The benchmark includes 1600+ questions over 180+ real-world environments.

claim_checks.notes: Repository exists; local execution was not attempted in this dry run.

paper_cards.limitations: It is an evaluation benchmark, not an interactive generation method; relevance is through downstream evaluation.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Useful as an evaluation branch reference for testing whether generated environments support meaningful embodied QA.

demo_cards.demo_notes: Paper page and linked ecosystem are available; exact runnable checkpoint status should be verified before permanent registry update.
Official project page provides benchmark overview and examples; no local reproduction attempted in dry-run.
